BiblicalUsage: The word is testimony, a witness bound up and sealed. Isaiah is told to bind up the testimony and seal the law among his disciples, and to speak according to the law and the testimony, for there is no light in those who speak not according to this word. In Ruth, the testimony of the sandal is the custom: a man plucked off his shoe and gave it to his neighbour, and this was a testimony in Israel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe testimony is meant to be bound up and kept, whether it is Isaiah's sealed word or a sandal changing hands. My position is that God's people live by the law and the testimony, and where those are silenced there is no light.
